newsitem.title: USA: USTR adds 200,000 tonnes raw cane sugar to quota.
newsitem.headline: USTR adds 200,000 tonnes raw cane sugar to quota.

text.p: The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Tuesday said it allocated an additional 200,000 tonnes of raw cane sugar for the fiscal yaer 1997 U.S. import quota.
U.S. Trade Representative-designate Charlene Barshefsky announced the country-by-country allocations that raise the fiscal 1997 quota to 1.9 million tonnes from 1.7 million.

Of the 40 participating countries, those with the largest quota increases announced today are the Dominican Republic, with an additional 35,736 tonnes; Brazil, with 29,442 tonnes; the Philippines, with 27,411; and Australia, with 16,853 tonnes.
The quota is adjusted in January, March and May and is based on the U.S. stocks-to-use ratio announced by the Agriculture Department.

If the ratio is 15.5 percent or less on the review dates, the quota automatically goes up 200,000 tonnes. If it is higher, the tranche is cancelled. Earlier today, the Agriculture Department estimated the stocks-to-use ratio at 14.0 percent.
